item.title: Corrigendum to "Well-posedness and regularity of the integral invariant model from linear scalar transport equation" [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 564 (2026) 130904]
item.description: arXiv:2611.28031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We clarify the compactly supported terminal test space and the moving-domain Bochner spaces in the integral invariant formulation. We complete the existence proof by establishing strong measurability and the initial trace, and replace the stability argument by a compact-test density argument that retains the original stability constant. A short appendix shows that the integral invariant identity remains valid for all square-integrable terminal test functions that vanish almost everywhere outside the terminal domain, thereby admitting the zero extensions of the cell polynomials used in the SLDG/SLFV method. We also correct the velocity and divergence in the swirling-deformation example.
item.dc:creator: Zhengrong Xie

item.title: Generalized Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg and related inequalities for Grushin-type gradients
item.description:
arXiv:2611.28253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for a generalized Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality involving the Grushin-type gradient $
abla_G=(
abla_x,|x|^\alpha
abla_y)$, where $\alpha\geq0$, in arbitrary dimensions. When $\alpha=0$, our results recover the classical Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequalities and extend the mixed radial and cylindrical weight inequalities of Li and Yan \cite{LY23} to arbitrary dimensions of the $y$ variables. Our approach combines a change of variables with approximation arguments to reduce the Grushin inequalities to Euclidean inequalities with mixed weights. We also characterize the admissible parameters in Hardy--Sobolev inequalities, including the endpoint cases $p=1$ and $q=p$, and derive multiplicative Sobolev and Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequalities. Finally, we establish a weighted Moser--Trudinger inequality on bounded domains and deduce exponential integrability for subcritical growth with arbitrary locally integrable cylindrical power weights. By letting $\alpha=0$, our results also yield the corresponding inequalities for the Euclidean gradient.
item.dc:creator: Trung Hieu Giang, Nguyen Minh Tri, Dang Anh Tuan

item.title: On the mode stability of a self-similar blow-up of Yang--Mills heat flow in five dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spectral stability properties of an explicitly known self-similar blowup profile to the Yang-Mills heat flow on $\mathbb R^5\times SO(5)$ often referred to as the Weinkove solution. We prove that this solution is mode stable in a dynamically evolving DeTurck gauge. To arrive at that result, we first reduce the problem to countably many vector-valued Schr\"odinger operators on the half line. We then proceed by proving uniform estimates for all but finitely many of said operators. The spectra of the remaining operators are studied individually by means of GGMT bounds or by comparison arguments. Two of these operators are distinguished as they have negative eigenvalues originating from symmetries. Among these two there is a scalar operator, previously analyzed by Donninger and Sch\"orkhuber, and an operator acting on a three-dimensional vector bundle. The latter operator's matrix structure prohibits a straightforward supersymmetric removal. To circumvent this, we transform the equation to a Schr\"odinger operator with drift terms to simplify the structure of the eigenfunction. We then develop tools to study such operators and conclude that said operator has no second negative eigenvalue.
item.dc:creator: Josef E. Greilhuber, David Wallauch

item.title: Nehari type characterizations of the mountain pass level on cones
item.description: arXiv:2611.28326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We relate the mountain pass level of a functional to its infimum over the part of the Nehari set formed by local maximizers of the fiber maps. {Unlike in the classical setting where every fiber map has a unique global maximizer,} the fiber maps need not all have a maximizer: working on each path-connected component of the cone of directions where they do, we show that the two levels coincide, for merely continuous functionals and without any compactness assumption. We also introduce a notion of mountain pass geometry with respect to a cone, which may hold when the classical one fails. {This geometry includes the zero-level case when a suitable separating set exists.} Under the Palais--Smale condition, each component carries a critical point at its own mountain pass level. Applications include indefinite and concave-convex problems with sign-changing weights, the affine $p$-Laplacian, nonlocal problems, and a problem related to the Fu\v{c}\'{\i}k spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Denilson S. Pereira, Humberto Ramos Quoirin, Jo\~ao R. Santos J\'unior, Kaye Silva

item.title: On the Planar Optimal Transport Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.28490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a complex analytic framework based on rotation of gradient graphs for the study of quadratic cost planar optimal transport with uniform densities. Using this framework we carry out the construction, characterization, and approximation of non-degenerate optimal transport maps up to the boundary. We also identify obstructions for continuous optimal transport and construct discontinuous optimal transport maps with prescribed analytic singular sets.
item.dc:creator: Arghya Rakshit, Aranya Sen

item.title: Asymptotic analysis and uniqueness of positive solutions to slightly subcritical fractional problems in symmetric domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.28503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the fractional Lane-Emden problem \[ (-\Delta)^s u = u^{p}\quad \text{ in }\Omega, \qquad u>0\quad \text{ in }\Omega, \qquad u=0 \text{ in }\mathbb R^N\setminus\Omega, \] admits a unique and nondegenerate solution when $\Omega$ is a smooth and bounded domain which is symmetric and convex with respect to $N$ orthogonal directions and the exponent $p$ is slightly subcritical. This result is new even in the case when $\Omega$ is a ball and $N\geq 2$. Our proof relies on a sharp characterization of the asymptotic behavior of low energy solutions, which we develop in general smooth bounded open sets.
item.dc:creator: Francesca De Marchis, Isabella Ianni, Alberto Salda\~na

item.title: Global well-posedness and scattering for the fractional inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrodinger equation with time-dependent damping
item.description: arXiv:2611.28530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove the global well-posedness and scattering of solutions for a nonlinear Schrodinger type equation with fractional Laplacian, inhomogeneous nonlinearity and time-dependent damping.We give an elementary proof based on Strichartz estimates combined with estimates of the nonlinear term in mixed-norm spaces. To avoid the loss of regularity in the Strichartz estimates, we consider the radial data.
item.dc:creator: Boyu Jiang, Kexue Li

item.title: Regularization for the inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in one dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.28561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the initial data problem for the following inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger (INLS) equation $$ i \partial_t u + \partial_x^2 u = \pm |x|^{-b} |u|^{2k} u, \quad u(0, x)= u_0(x),$$ where $b>0$ and $k\in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$. The singular potential $|x|^{-b}$ impairs the Sobolev regularity that can be propagated by the flow. We establish the regularization mechanism of this model and prove local well-posedness in $H_x^{\alpha}$ for $\alpha=5/2-b-$. Moreover, at the endpoint space $H_x^{5/2-b}$, we show that there is no $C^{2k+1}$ flow map at the origin. The proof combines the one-dimensional local smoothing effect with a normal-form reduction for the high-low interaction generated by the singular part of the coefficient. The argument applies to both the focusing and defocusing cases.
item.dc:creator: Ruobing Bai, Luccas Campos, Cui Ning

item.title: Finsler--Sobolev inequalities: optimality & rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.28624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish optimal Sobolev and logarithmic-Sobolev inequalities on non-compact, possibly non-reversible Finsler manifolds with non-negative weighted Ricci curvature. The optimal constants exhibit no dependence on reversibility -- confirming Ohta's conjectural principle -- being governed solely by the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios. We then apply the logarithmic-Sobolev inequality to establish the optimal hypercontractivity estimate for the heat flow in the same geometric setting. The equality cases of the above optimal inequalities imply strong rigidity in the underlying manifold, characterized by fine properties of the flag and $S$-curvatures as well as the precise profiles of the corresponding extremizers. We illustrate our results by examples including Randers metrics obtained by Zermelo navigation with Killing vector fields, and weighted convex cones in $\mathbb{R}^n$ endowed with arbitrary Minkowski norms, the latter showing that the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios may differ.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Krist\'aly

item.title: Global existence and decay estimates for classical solutions to 2D compressible micropolar fluid equations with vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2611.28657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluid equations with far field vacuum. Under the assumption that the initial energy is sufficiently small, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong and classical solutions, allowing for large oscillations in the initial data. The key to the proof is to derive {\it a priori} decay estimates for the pressure, the velocity gradient, and the microrotational velocity, which enable us to close the bootstrap argument. We also handle the difficulties arising from the coupling between the velocity field and the microrotational velocity.
item.dc:creator: Guo Houbin, Zhu Changjiang, Zhu Qiaolong

item.title: Weak-type bow shocks
item.description: arXiv:2611.28698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An existence proof is given for bow shocks ahead of blunt convex wedges that are transonic and of weak type at infinity, including cases for arbitrarily small shock strength. It is also proven that any such flow is necessarily univalent, meaning the position-to-velocity map is injective.
item.dc:creator: Volker Wilhelm Elling

item.title: Nonlinear Stability of Two-Dimensional Poiseuille Flow via a Dilation Multiplier
item.description: arXiv:2611.28750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate nonlinear stability of the Poiseuille flow for 2D incompressible Navier Stokes equations.The key observation is that, after Fourier transformation, the Poiseuille flow and its curvature give rise to a kinetic operator and a potential whose commutators with the same bounded dilation multiplier are both nonnegative.To close the nonlinear estimates, we incorporate the zero mode of the initial velocity into the background shear flow, thereby further improving the threshold.
item.dc:creator: Nangao Zhang

item.title: Improved Singular Adams-type inequalities and the existence of extremals in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:2611.28866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $H_0^2(\Omega)$ denote the Sobolev space on $\Omega$, where $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ is a smooth bounded domain containing the origin, and let $\lambda(\Omega)$ denote the first eigenvalue of the bi-Laplacian $\Delta^2$ on $\Omega$ subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. We establish the following singular Adams inequality of Adimurthi-Druet type: for $0<\beta<4$ and $0\leq\alpha<\lambda(\Omega)$, \[ \sup\limits_{{u\in H_0^2(\Omega),\|\Delta u\|_2^2=1}}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) u^2(1+\alpha\|u\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx < +\infty. \] Moreover, this supremum is infinite for $\alpha>\lambda_1(\Omega)$. Furthermore, we show the existence of extremal functions, that is, for sufficiently small $\alpha>0$, there exists $u^*\in H_0^2(\Omega)\cap C_{\mathrm{loc}}^4(\Omega\setminus{0})$ with $\|\Delta u^*\|_2^2=1$ such that \[ \int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) {|u^*|}^2(1+\alpha\|u^*\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx=\sup\limits_{{u\in H_0^2(\Omega),\|\Delta u\|_2^2=1}}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) u^2(1+\alpha\|u\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx. \] These results can be regarded as a further development, in the singular setting, of the theory on the existence of extremals established by Lu and Yang [Adv. Math. (2009)]. Our proof relies on the blow-up analysis of the subcritical maximizers, combined with biharmonic truncation adapted to the singular weight, capacity-type estimates on annular regions and a test function argument. A key novelty of our approach lies in carrying out the blow-up analysis without relying on an explicit expression for the limiting profile near the blow-up point, which is unavailable in the present setting. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to perform such a blow-up analysis without the explicit form of the limiting profile.
item.dc:creator: Xumin Wang, Maochun Zhu

item.title: Weak-Weak Stability for Multi-Species Nonlocal Cross-Diffusion Systems with Endpoint Lorentz Kernels
item.description: arXiv:2611.28932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantitative weak-weak stability for multi-species nonlocal cross-diffusion systems on the torus is established. The interactions of the species are described by a symmetric, positive semidefinite matrix-valued kernel whose gradient belongs to the endpoint Lorentz space $L^{d,\infty}$, where $d\ge 2$ is the space dimension. The central estimate, formulated in terms of a modulated Hellinger distance-interaction energy, yields uniqueness of solutions with finite Boltzmann entropy and Fisher information. The proof relies on a two-level endpoint mechanism: The Boltzmann entropy controls the interaction energy, while the Fisher information controls the associated force field. Further results are the immediate $L^2$ regularization and the exponential decay to the homogeneous equilibrium. As a particular application, uniqueness and stability for the two-dimensional Poisson-Nernst-Planck system with periodic Coulomb kernels are obtained.
item.dc:creator: Ansgar J\"ungel, Tuan Tung Nguyen, Zhiwei Sun

item.title: Fractional order Orlicz--Sobolev spaces revisited
item.description: arXiv:2611.28950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this paper is to revisit our work [J. Funct. Anal. 277 (2019), 333--367], where fractional order Orlicz--Sobolev spaces were introduced and their behavior as the fractional parameter $s\uparrow1$ was studied, and to redo it without assuming the $\Delta_2$ condition on the Young function $G$ or on its complementary function. Since that paper appeared, the theory of these spaces has been considerably developed, and the tools available today allow for a cleaner treatment in full generality. We prove a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type formula as $s\uparrow1$, a compactness and lower semicontinuity result for sequences with bounded energy, a Poincar\'e inequality uniform in $s$, and the $\Gamma$-convergence of the fractional modulars to a local modular on arbitrary open sets. As an application we study the asymptotic behavior of minimizers and of solutions of Dirichlet problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian as $s\uparrow1$. This version also corrects some errors in the original paper, and it is intended to serve as a more complete and reliable reference for these results.
item.dc:creator: Julian Fernandez Bonder, Ariel Salort

item.title: Convergence analysis of resonant frequency approximation in periodic Helmholtz problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.29023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate resonant frequencies of the Helmholtz equation in periodic structures under quasi-periodic conditions, using approximations of the associated quasi-periodic Green function, which is represented by a lattice sum. By formulating the periodic Helmholtz problem using layer potential operators whose kernel is given by the quasi-periodic Green function, resonant frequencies correspond to characteristic values of an associated operator-valued function. Based on two approximation methods for the quasi-periodic Green function, the Ewald method and the shifted Green function method, we propose the corresponding approximation schemes for resonant frequencies. Furthermore, we establish convergence rates for the resulting approximations using Gohberg--Sigal theory, where the Ewald method yields exponential convergence, while the shifted Green function method yields algebraic convergence. Numerical computations are presented to validate and compare the proposed approximation schemes.
item.dc:creator: Jiho Hong, Woojoo Lee, Mikyoung Lim

item.title: Stability of a Paraboloidal Steady Solution for the 2D Surface Growth Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.29076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we consider the stability problem of 2D surface growth model. To be specific, we prove that the small perturbation of the paraboloidal steady solution decays to zero in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^2)$. The decay occurs both for the perturbation and its gradient, whose decay rates are $O(t^{-1/2})$ and $O(t^{-1}\log t)$, respectively. The proof is based on the linearization of the perturbation equation and the bootstrap argument to close the statement in nonlinear equation. Sufficient conditions for stability require the initial data and its gradient of the perturbation to be small in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and Wiener algebra $\mathcal{A}$. It is notable that the smallness in second derivative is not necessary, which is physically reasonable because large second derivative would lead to high surface energy and it is expected to be relaxed in short time. We also prove existence and uniqueness of mild solution for perturbation equation under those conditions.
item.dc:creator: Won-Suk Lee

item.title: Weighted Carleson embedding on product of trees in general dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.29082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the equivalence of the Carleson embedding on $n$-trees (arbitrary Cartesian product of trees) and the box condition, for arbitrary nonnegative measures and generalized product weights. For product weights, we obtain the sharp coefficient $4^n$. This extends the bi-tree and tri-tree embedding theorems of \cite{AMPVZ} and \cite{MPVZ} to every dimension. We also give two applications of the Carleson embedding: we characterize Carleson measures for the classical Dirichlet space on the polydisc $\mathbb D^n$ and deduce criteria for bounded composition operators from this space into weighted Bergman spaces, generalizing the results from \cite{MPVZ} and \cite{Beslikas2025}. Finally, we define a generalized logarithmic Dirichlet space and characterize its Carleson measures.
item.dc:creator: Michail Paparizos, Georgios Psaromiligkos

item.title: Local and Global Bifurcation for Axisymmetric Stationary Relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell Equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2611.29153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study bifurcation of stationary two-species relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell equilibria on bounded axisymmetric domains. Velocity-moment and elliptic spectral bounds give computable tests for simple crossings, their number and separation, while the local theorem gives a branch-direction formula. Explicit two-species families exhibit electric-only, magnetic-only, and joint field-norm escape.
item.dc:creator: Katherine Zhiyuan Zhang

item.title: Principal Eigenvalues for Transport-Nonlocal Operators on Compact Manifolds: Ergodic Averages and Quotient Reduction
item.description: arXiv:2611.29159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study principal eigenvalues for transport--nonlocal operators on connected compact Riemannian manifolds. Transport changes the natural spectral threshold from the pointwise maximum of the potential to a maximal invariant average. We establish a necessary and sufficient criterion based on a resolvent spectral radius and derive sufficient existence conditions for uniquely ergodic flows and, through quotient reduction, for flows arising from compact abelian Lie group actions. Examples on the two-dimensional torus show that, for weak nonlocal coupling, transport can create or suppress principal eigenvalues, while sphere rotations illustrate how the quotient criterion accommodates singular orbits.
item.dc:creator: Xing Liang, Lei Zhang, Niansen Zhang

item.title: Split Hamiltonian structure for Vlasov--Maxwell equations and cylindrical pinch equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2611.29164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the linearized Vlasov--Maxwell equations for cylindrical pinch equilibria, including the classical Bennett pinch, Gaussian equilibria from our earlier work, and a rigidly rotating $\theta$-pinch. Conservation of particle momentum along a symmetry brings the energy principle of Lin and Strauss into these geometries. We work on a graph space for the symmetry component of the vector potential. For the Bennett $z$-pinch the bare potential form has one negative direction, but the particle-number constraint removes it and the entire $z$-independent spectrum lies on the imaginary axis. For a $z$-pinch with variable axial drift, every $z$-independent growing mode is radial. We prove axisymmetric spectral stability for a Gaussian $\theta$-pinch in an explicit range of axis slopes and for a center-peaked, rigidly rotating $\theta$-pinch. In a screw-pinch the helical twist couples the magnetic flux to the particle and electric constraints. The radial equations still separate, and all sufficiently high helical harmonics have imaginary spectrum. For two Gaussian screw-pinch equilibria we verify spectral stability in the full helical symmetry class.
item.dc:creator: Justin Holmer, Katherine Zhiyuan Zhang

item.title: Accidental Threefold Dirac Points at the Origin of the Brillouin Zone and Wave-Packet Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.29203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study accidental threefold degeneracies at zero quasimomentum for scalar periodic wave operators on the square lattice. At an isolated positive triple eigenvalue, the middle Bloch band has zero linear term. The two outer bands open linearly in every direction precisely when a Gram matrix of coupling coefficients is positive definite. Square symmetry makes the resulting cone isotropic. For weak perturbations of a constant medium, we construct two transverse tuning curves on which a singlet coincides with a doublet away from their common origin. The central band has positive quadratic curvature along each coordinate axis. For a dilute inclusion of size $\eta$, a variational gap condition gives a unique transverse crossing in a contrast interval of order $\eta^{-2}\log(1/\eta)$. The crossing frequency is asymptotic to $\sqrt{2\pi/\log(1/\eta)}$, and the cone speed vanishes linearly with $\eta$, with a coefficient determined by the far-field dipole moment. A three-component Dirac equation approximates positive-frequency wave packets with an error bound explicit in the material coefficients and the spectral separation at zero quasimomentum. When the singlet has nonzero cell mean, the response to a uniform cell source yields effective permittivity and permeability with simple zeros at the crossing frequency. We express their slopes in terms of the singlet mean and the cone speed. The resulting bulk impedance tends to zero in a weak-contrast example and grows inversely with the inclusion size in the dilute high-contrast crystal.
item.dc:creator: Habib Ammari, Xin Fu, Bowen Li

item.title: Combined quasi-neutral and zero-relaxation limit of Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system
item.description: arXiv:2611.29221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the combined quasi-neutral and zero-relaxation limit of Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system. With well-prepared initial, we show that the convergence from Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system for electron and Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system for ion to the incompressible Euler equations and compressible Euler equations, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Li, Xianwen Zhang

item.title: Global large-data strong solutions to the 2D barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with linear bulk viscosity
item.description: arXiv:2611.29247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper concerns the global well-posedness of the two-dimensional(2D) compressible Navier--Stokes equations with density-dependent bulk viscosity and far-field vacuum. We consider the constitutive laws \(P(\rho)=\rho^\gamma\), with \(\gamma>1\), and \(\lambda(\rho)=\rho\), for which the bulk viscosity degenerates in vacuum. Under suitable regularity and weighted integrability assumptions on the initial data, and assuming only that the total mass is positive, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions without any restriction on the size of the initial energy or any radial symmetry assumption. The central difficulty is to derive an upper bound for the density on arbitrary finite time intervals in the absence of enhanced bulk dissipation. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a logarithmic energy method based on successive density levels, which exploits the dissipation accumulated along particle trajectories as the density increases. Combined with weighted estimates, pressure estimates, and the analysis of the effective viscous flux and vorticity, this method yields the density bound required to close the global continuation argument. Our result extends the large-data global strong-solution theory for density-dependent viscosity to the critical linear bulk-viscosity law in the general two-dimensional whole-space setting.
item.dc:creator: Qian Li, Zhilei Liang, Zhuan Ye

item.title: Persistence and Breakdown of the Initial Gaussian Rate Function for 1D Quasi-Periodic Cubic NLS
item.description: arXiv:2611.29251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study rare events for the spatial supremum of the solution amplitude in the 1D cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with weak nonlinearity and Gaussian quasi-periodic initial data.Under suitable polynomial decay assumptions in Fourier space and a Diophantine condition controlling small divisors arising from spatial quasi-periodicity, we prove that the initial Gaussian rate function persists uniformly on the \emph{critical logarithmic correction time scale} with a \emph{small enough} prefactor. Using the \emph{Akhmediev breather}, we obtain that the same Gaussian rate function \emph{fails} to hold uniformly on this time scale with a \emph{large} prefactor. This also implies that the initial Gaussian rate function cannot, in general, persist uniformly on arbitrarily long polynomial time scales.
item.dc:creator: Fei Xu (Jilin University), Yong Li (Jilin University)

item.title: Strict hot spots and absence of interior critical points on simply connected planar H\"older domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.29324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove strict hot spots and the absence of interior critical points for every nonzero real eigenfunction at the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of a bounded simply connected planar H\"older domain. The H\"older hypothesis is the quasihyperbolic boundary condition; equivalently, the derivative of a Riemann map belongs to $L^p$ for some $p>2$. The eigenvalue may be multiple, and the boundary need not be Jordan; boundary extrema are then interpreted through the continuous conformal pullback. The theorem includes bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains, polygonal Jordan domains with reentrant corners, bounded convex domains, simply connected John domains, and quasidisks. We extend the reciprocal Green kernel method for smooth domains by constructing boundary primitives for the transformed Neumann gradient and proving a multiplier estimate uniform under conformal exhaustion. Approximation of the whole limiting eigenspace handles splitting of a multiple eigenvalue.
item.dc:creator: Yutian Li

item.title: Stability of Viscous Shock Waves of the Compressible Navier-Stokes System with Large Initial Perturbation
item.description: arXiv:2611.29329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show in this paper that viscous shock waves of the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations are time-asymptotically nonlinear stable with large initial perturbation. While results for small initial data are well-established, the case of large initial perturbations remains less satisfactory. As far as we know, only under a class of large initial perturbations, the asymptotical stability of weak viscous shock wave was derived. In this work, we will provide a complete resolution of this problem for weak viscous shock wave. The key idea involves combining the $a$-contraction with shifts theory with a time splitting method to obtain the weighted $L^2$ estimates, which enables us to derive uniform upper and lower bounds on the specific volume. Our method can be also applied to proving the nonlinear stability of composite waves.
item.dc:creator: Lan Zhang, Huijiang Zhao

item.title: The fundamental solution of the logarithmic Laplacian is a function in dimensions 1 and 2
item.description: arXiv:2611.29345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the fundamental solution of the logarithmic Laplacian in dimensions $1$ and $2$ is a locally integrable function. Together with earlier work of the first author, this resolves a conjecture of Chen and V\'eron. The key step is that the inverse Fourier transform of the high-frequency part of $1/\log(|\xi|^2)$ behaves like $|x|^{-d}(\log(1/|x|))^{-2}$ near the origin.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Killick, David Lee

item.title: On fourteen problems in the theory of composites
item.description: arXiv:2611.29402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study fourteen questions of Milton on the effective properties of composites. For one scalar potential every effective tensor of two fixed planar phases has a laminate representative. Two coupled potentials suffice for failure. In space, dyadic resistor networks characterize the isotropic conductivity closure, and some laws in it have no finite-perimeter periodic representative. We construct intervals on the single-pole absorption arc and hole-free planar inclusions realizing optimal double-coating laws. For a solid with void or perfectly rigid inclusions we characterize the two- and three-dimensional tensor closures. Porous solids can approach full shear at vanishing bulk in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. Prescribing a finite planar shortening gives a sharp loss of initial shear. We give the complete shear interval at each bulk for a polycrystal. For two positive elastic phases, changing only the bulk moduli can reverse which dimension admits a shear common to every attainable bulk.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Bogdan

item.title: An Annular Spiral Construction for Anomalous Dissipation in the Forced Navier-Stokes Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.29458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kolmogorov's 1941 theory of turbulence (K41) predicts that the rate of kinetic energy dissipation in a turbulent flow can remain positive as viscosity tends to zero. In 2023, Bru\`e and De Lellis used quasi-self-similar mixing to construct solutions of the forced three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations exhibiting anomalous dissipation. In this paper, we show that anomalous dissipation can still occur for a flow with spiral geometry in an annulus. In the horizontal plane, we wind a radial segment into a two-turn spiral and then apply alternating shears. After each pair of shears, the image of the segment shares a subarc of positive length with the original spiral. We compare the vertical velocity with sine profiles whose angular period halves with each pair. After the horizontal flow stops, diffusion damps the final profile. By embedding this planar construction into the $(2+\frac{1}{2})$-dimensional framework, we obtain smooth solutions of the three-dimensional equations with the same smooth initial datum. For a sequence of viscosities tending to zero, their dissipation over a fixed subannulus and one vertical period has a uniform positive lower bound, and their forces converge in $C^\alpha$ uniformly in time for every $0<\alpha<1$. We use this spiral construction to produce solutions of the forced three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations that exhibit anomalous dissipation.
item.dc:creator: Changhong Li

item.title: A near-quadratic bound for critical sets of harmonic functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.29500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $u$ be a nonconstant harmonic function in $B_1 \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with $n \ge 3$. Denote by $N$ the doubling index of $|\nabla u|$ in $B_1$. Let $\mathcal{C} := \{ x\in B_1: \nabla u(x) = 0 \}$ be the critical set. We show that $$\mathcal{H}^{n-2}(\mathcal{C} \cap B_{1/2}) \le C_n N^2 \log^2(N+2).$$ This estimate is sharp up to a squared logarithm loss.
item.dc:creator: Zhongwei Shen, Jinping Zhuge

item.title: A necessary and sufficient condition for steady Euler flows to be shear flows in an infinite strip
item.description: arXiv:2611.29514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a necessary and sufficient characterization of parallel shear flows among all $C^1$ steady incompressible Euler flows in an infinite strip, subject to the slip boundary condition. We show that a steady Euler flow is a parallel shear flow if and only if almost every regular streamline traverses the strip longitudinally. The proof relies on three key ingredients. First, the topological assumption on the streamlines yields global bounds on the stream function, the velocity, and the vorticity. Second, we establish a novel geometric formula for the total curvature which, together with the topological assumption on the streamlines, implies the finiteness of the total curvature via the area and coarea formulas. Third, once the total curvature is finite, we derive the asymptotic behavior of the flow in the far field, which in turn forces the total curvature to vanish.
item.dc:creator: Changfeng Gui, Xiaofan Wang, Huan Xu, Wen Yang

item.title: Sixth-Order Q-Curvature of Conformally Euclidean Metrics: Improved Dimensional Thresholds, Quantitative Lower Bounds and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.29534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the sign of the sixth-order \(Q\)-curvature of conformally Euclidean metrics on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) for integers \(n\ge2m\) and \(m\ge4\). Under suitable assumptions, we refine the sixfold integral estimates and prove that \(Q_g^{(6)}>0\) whenever \(2m\le n\le4m-6+[\widehat h_m]\), where \(\widehat h_m\) is the unique positive root of \(G_m\) and \(\widehat h_m\sim\frac{2\sqrt7-4}{3}m\) as \(m\to\infty\). Moreover, we strengthen this positivity result by establishing the quantitative lower bound \(Q_g^{(6)}(x)\ge\Theta_{m,n}\bigl(Q_g^{(2)}(x)\bigr)^3>0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), where \(\Theta_{m,n}>0\) is an explicit constant depending only on \(m\) and \(n\). These quantitative inequalities also yield explicit lower bounds for intermediate Laplacians in higher-order elliptic equations. On the non-positivity side, we construct metrics satisfying \(Q_g^{(6)}(0)<0\) whenever \(n>\widetilde N_m\), where \(\widetilde N_m\sim\widetilde\Lambda m\) as \(m\to\infty\) and \(\widetilde\Lambda\simeq9.74268\). These metrics extend smoothly to \(\mathbb S^n\) and are conformal to the round metric. In the same dimensional range, we further construct metrics with \(Q_g^{(6)}(0)>0\) and establish uniform positive lower and upper bounds for \(Q_g^{(2m)}\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). Our results extend the positivity range and lower the counterexample threshold obtained by V\'etois and Zeitler (arXiv preprint, 2026). The sixth-order estimate also answers a question raised in our previous work on quantitative fourth-order \(Q\)-curvature bounds. These results provide new insights into Conjecture 1 of Li and Xu (J. Funct. Anal. 289 (2025), 111011) in the case \(k=3\), clarifying its validity and limitations across different dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Jianlun Liu, Hong-Rui Sun, Ziheng Zhang

item.title: Concentration in Hardy equations and singular heat flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.29540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the stability and loss of concentrated source data in critical Hardy equations and in singular heat flows. For the critical local Hardy form, a dyadic condition on the radial marginal characterizes admissibility and strong energy convergence under a uniform bound on angular densities. For general diffuse measures at inverse power one, strong convergence is characterized by mass convergence and condenser-capacity discrepancies. We also establish sharp moment inequalities and tightness criteria for the radial pole trace and boundary slope. At the sharp fractional $L^p$ Hardy coefficient, we identify the pole flux in a nonlinear power balance and show that finite remainder excludes nonconstant strong angular traces. For every fractional order, positive data can have finite remainder but infinite source pairing. Finally, for singular heat reactions with a positive nonincreasing factor tending to zero at infinity, we determine all attainable reaction limits of a time impulse and of data exhausted by parabolic Kato measures. A total variation estimate describes the combination of these mechanisms for countably many impulses.
item.dc:creator: Masoud Bayrami

item.title: Global topology and symmetry breaking in an indefinite superlinear Dirichlet problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.29550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the work of Fencl and L\'opez-G\'omez [13] on global bifurcation diagrams, we study the connected components of positive solutions of $-u''=\lambda u+a(x)u^p$ on $(-1,1)$ with $u(-1)=u(1)=0$, where $a$ changes sign and $p\ge2$ is an integer. For generic $\mathcal C^r$ weights, $r\ge2$, with $n$ positive intervals, simple zeros and negative endpoint values, we obtain at least $2^{n-1}$ noncompact components. Apart from the principal component, each is a curve with both ends at $\lambda=-\infty$. The proof distinguishes at least $2^n-1$ ends and yields bounds for branching and compactly supported cohomology. For even weights, an odd Morse index of at least $k$ on the principal symmetric component forces at least $k$ symmetry-breaking points. In particular, symmetry breaking occurs if $a(0)<0$.
item.dc:creator: Juan Carlos Sampedro

item.title: Hessian type equations with gradient source term and measure data
item.description: arXiv:2611.29562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of nonnegative solutions to $F_k[-u]=|Du|^q\,dx+t\mu$ for some $t>0$, where $\mu$ is a finite nonnegative measure on $\mathbb{R}^N$. We consider the whole space $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $2\leq k<\frac{N}{2}$ and $q>\frac{Nk}{N-k}$, and a bounded domain $\Omega$ with $2\leq k<N$ and $q>k$. We also establish pointwise gradient estimates in terms of the Wolff potential.
item.dc:creator: Shiguang Ma, Zijian Wang

item.title: Approximate controllability in Sobolev spaces of periodic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with bilinear controls
item.description: arXiv:2611.29569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the torus $\T^d$ with a smooth real-valued potential and nonlinearity $\kappa|\psi|^{2p}\psi$, where the dimension $d\ge1$, the integer $p\ge1$, and the coefficient $\kappa\in\R$ are arbitrary. The controls act bilinearly through finitely many low Fourier modes. For every integer $s>d/2$, we prove approximate controllability in $H^s$ between any two nowhere vanishing states on the unit sphere in $L^2$ at any prescribed positive time. The proof combines small-time phase control, a transport approximation in $H^s$, and a construction of short uncontrolled trajectories connecting states with different winding vectors.
item.dc:creator: Vahagn Nersesyan

item.title: On the splitting of fractional Dirichlet eigenvalues in perforated domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.29580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of eigenvalues of the fractional Laplacian under singular domain perturbations produced by the removal of a hole with vanishing fractional capacity. First, we establish an expansion formula for eigenbranches bifurcating from a possibly multiple eigenvalue. We then investigate splitting phenomena: specifically, removing a family of holes concentrating at a zero-capacity compact set (lying outside a closed set of measure zero) causes a multiple eigenbranch to split into branches of smaller multiplicity. Finally, for holes concentrating at a point, we prove that the largest eigenbranch generically detaches from the rest and becomes simple.
item.dc:creator: Veronica Felli, Prasun Roychowdhury, Giovanni Siclari

item.title: Liouville systems II: Critical points at infinity in the resonant case
item.description: arXiv:2611.29595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a Liouville system at a resonant parameter, we construct a bounded, locally Lipschitz pseudogradient, which classifies the non-compact ends of its flow at finite energy levels. If the reduced functional is Morse and the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical pair, each unbounded forward trajectory with energy bounded below converges in the bubbling parameters to a pair with negative coefficient. Conversely, each such pair, up to a permutation, is realized by an open set of escaping trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Mohameden Ahmedou, Jonas Fey, Zhengni Hu, Lei Zhang

item.title: Leray's Problem for the Stationary Navier-Stokes Equations with Low-Regularity Data in Planar and Three-Dimensional Axisymmetric Lipschitz Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.29707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the steady Navier-Stokes Dirichlet problem in bounded planar and three-dimensional axisymmetric domains with finitely many disjoint Lipschitz boundary components. For prescribed velocities in $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ and forces in the dual of the solenoidal energy space $V=H_0^1(\operatorname{div}0,\Omega)$, we establish finite-energy solvability under the sole compatibility condition of zero total boundary flux. Individual component fluxes are subject to no smallness or sign restrictions. In three dimensions the domain and data are axisymmetric, and swirl is allowed. The result addresses the regularity of the domain and data within these two geometric classes. The proof combines Leray-Schauder continuation with pressure compactness on Lipschitz boundary collars and a total-head level-set argument. Continuation of the limiting Euler fields through complementary components supplies separating cycles, while viscous identities are evaluated inside the physical domain. A nonlinear correction of smooth force approximations controls the volume and surface errors in the passage to energy-dual data. An isometric extension from $V'$ to $H^{-1}$ preserves the prescribed symmetries and fixes the force representative used in the compactness argument. For each selected $H^{-1}$ representative, the resulting velocity admits an associated mean-zero $L^2$ pressure; the velocity equation depends only on the force class modulo gradients.
item.dc:creator: Zhibing Zhang

item.title: Global classification and local asymptotics for a Monge-Amp\`{e}re obstacle problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.29855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n\geq2$ and $0<q<n$. We prove that every nontrivial convex entire solution of $$\det D^2v = v^q, \quad v \geq 0, \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^n$$ with bounded (possibly empty) coincidence set $\{v=0\}$ is affine equivalent to a radial solution. Together with the classification for unbounded coincidence sets by Jin-Tu-Xiong \cite{JTX2025}, this completes the classification of nontrivial nonnegative convex entire solutions. The proof uses an affine-invariant monotonicity formula extending the two-dimensional formula in Mooney-Sen \cite{MooneySen2026}. Combining this global classification with level-set parametrization and spectral analysis, we also obtain precise asymptotics of local solutions at isolated zeros, settling the remaining case, namely, a singleton free boundary, in the regularity theory for the Monge-Amp\`{e}re obstacle problem studied in \cite{JTX2025}.
item.dc:creator: Tianling Jin, Connor Mooney, Aranya Sen, Xushan Tu, Jingang Xiong

item.title: Global strong solvability of the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes equations for large initial data
item.description: arXiv:2611.29893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1995, Kazhikhov and Vaigant introduced a two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes model with constant shear viscosity and bulk viscosity $\lambda(\rho)=\rho^\beta$. For $\beta>3$, they proved global existence of smooth solutions for arbitrarily large initial data with strictly positive density. More recently, Fan-Jiang-Li-L\"u (arXiv:2611.20264, 2026) proved global strong solvability for every $\beta>1$ in bounded simply connected domains with Navier-slip boundary conditions. In this article, we prove global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to the Kazhikhov-Vaigant model on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ at the critical point $\beta=1$, for every $\gamma>1$ and arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum.
item.dc:creator: Jie Fan, Xiangdi Huang, Muxi Lei

item.title: Blow-up phenomena and ill-posedness for the 2D Euler-Poincar\'e equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.29927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study finite-time blow-up and critical norm inflation for the Euler--Poincar\'e equations on $\mathbb R^2$. We consider a class of momentum fields admitting the div--curl decomposition with radial scalar potentials. The potentials satisfy a nonlocal transport system. By virtue of the conservation law and the finite propagation speed property, we obtain a growth estimate for the potential, which yields a sufficient condition for finite-time blow-up. Furthermore, combining a multiscale construction of the initial data with a blow-up criterion formulated in terms of the Besov norm of the deformation tensor, we establish norm inflation at the zero initial datum in $H^2(\mathbb R^2)$, thereby proving ill-posedness in this critical Sobolev space.
item.dc:creator: Wei Luo, Zhaoyang Yin, Pei Zheng

item.title: Space-time almost periodicity for the defocusing NLS hierarchy via local Toeplitz operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.29931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the defocusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger hierarchy for reflectionless initial data with Dirac spectrum $E$. Under a gap moment condition of order $m$ and the assumption that $E$ is homogeneous, we prove existence and space-time almost periodicity of a global classical solution through order $m$ for every such initial datum. More generally, it suffices that $\mathbb C\setminus E$ be a Dirichlet regular Widom domain satisfying the direct Cauchy theorem and that the gap maxima of a weighted Green potential be summable, in addition to the gap moment condition. We obtain the frequencies by summing the upper and lower boundary values of the corrected powers $z^r$ on each gap and use local Toeplitz operators to reconstruct the potential from the gap phases. We also prove uniqueness under bounds on the spatial derivatives.
item.dc:creator: Shuo Zhang

item.title: Global existence and large-time behavior of classical axisymmetric solutions to the two-dimensional viscous Saint-Venant equations and related models
item.description: arXiv:2611.29974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes system with density-dependent viscosity in a disk, subject to the no-slip boundary condition. We consider both the symmetric viscous stress and the stress written in terms of the full velocity gradient. In each case the coefficients satisfy the BD relation $\mu(\rho)=\rho^\alpha$ and $\lambda(\rho)=2(\alpha-1)\rho^\alpha$. For every $1/2<\alpha\le1$ and $\gamma>1$, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for arbitrarily large axisymmetric initial data with strictly positive density and possibly nonzero tangential velocity. Moreover, the density has upper and positive lower bounds independent of time, and the solution converges to the constant equilibrium. The two stresses give the same radial momentum equation, but require different estimates of the tangential velocity. The endpoint $\alpha=1$, $\gamma=2$ includes the viscous shallow-water equations.
item.dc:creator: Xiangdi Huang, Muxi Lei, Weili Meng

item.title: Growth versus boundedness for viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations with a forcing term: a Fujita-type dichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2611.30060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t=\Delta u+|\nabla u|^q+a(t)w(x)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, where $q>1$ and the integrable forcing has positive total mass. Unlike classical Fujita problems, regular solutions exist globally, so the relevant dichotomy concerns boundedness versus grow-up. We identify the critical exponent $q_c=N/(N-1)$ for $N\geq 2$, with $q_c=\infty$ for $N=1$. For stationary forcing, every solution grows at least linearly on a fixed ball when $1<q\leq q_c$. In two dimensions, solutions tend to infinity locally uniformly for every $q>1$, with an explicit logarithmic lower bound. For $q=2$, the Cole--Hopf transformation relates the exact growth rate to the spectrum of $-\Delta-w$. Conversely, when $N\geq 3$ and $q>q_c$, bounded solutions exist for sufficiently small nonnegative data and forcing. We also establish growth criteria for time-dependent forcing, including decaying profiles.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Castillo, Mohamed Majdoub

item.title: The first Fu\v{c}\'ik curve of the $p$-Laplacian on compact quantum graphs: slopes at the diagonal and nonresonance
item.description: arXiv:2611.30186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Fu\v{c}\'{\i}k spectrum of the $p$-Laplacian, $1<p<\infty$, on a compact connected quantum graph, with Dirichlet conditions on a possibly empty set $V_D$ of vertices whose removal does not disconnect the graph and Kirchhoff conditions at the others. We construct the first nontrivial curve $\mathfrak C$ of the spectrum by a mountain pass argument and show that it is Lipschitz and strictly decreasing. As the parameter tends to infinity, $\mathfrak C$ tends to the first eigenvalue if $V_D\neq\emptyset$, and otherwise to the smallest first eigenvalue obtained by a Dirichlet condition at a single point. If the second eigenvalue is simple, we compute the two one-sided slopes of $\mathfrak C$ at the diagonal. The curve is differentiable there if and only if the positive and negative parts of the second eigenfunction have the same $L^p$ norm. On three-edge stars these norms differ for suitable edge lengths and every $p$, so the Lipschitz regularity is optimal. For $p=2$ the simplicity assumption can be dropped, and for a simple eigenvalue the corner is the crossing of the two smooth branches of the spectrum through the diagonal point. Finally, we prove a nonresonance result in which, for $V_D=\emptyset$, the ratio $f(x,s)/|s|^{p-2}s$ may be arbitrarily large at $+\infty$, provided it stays below the threshold at $-\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Archana Prajapati, Divya Goel

item.title: Existence and multiplicity of radial solutions for higher order logarithmic and infinite mass Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.30251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study radial solutions of the Schr\"odinger equation $-\Delta u+V(x)u=g(u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge3$, where $V$ is radial and $g(t)/t\to-\infty$ as $t\to0$. In this infinite-mass case the energy functional is not finite on $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$. First let $g(t)=t|\log|t||^{\alpha-1}\log|t|$ with $\alpha>1$. We only assume that $V$ is continuous and bounded from below. So $V$ may change sign, and it need not be coercive or have a limit at infinity. We obtain a nontrivial radial solution and a sequence of radial solutions whose energies tend to infinity. To do this, we add the term $\lambda|u|^{p-2}u$ with $1<p<2$, find critical points of the perturbed functional by minimax methods, and let $\lambda\to0$. The infinite-mass structure gives the compactness in this limit. Next let $g$ be odd, with a power bound near zero and at most critical growth at infinity. Let $V$ be bounded, with a smallness condition on $(x\cdot\nabla V)_+$. We combine the Pohozaev identity with an augmented symmetric minimax method and obtain infinitely many pairs of radial solutions. A negative critical power term is allowed.
item.dc:creator: Chen Huang, Rong Li, Junren Luo, Xian Zhang

item.title: Principal spectral theory of time-periodic nonlocal advective cooperative systems and its applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.30262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a new spectral theory for time-periodic nonlocal cooperative systems with advection on bounded intervals, allowing asymmetric dispersal kernels. By transforming the problem into a nonlocal moving-boundary problem, we show that the associated Poincar\'e map is strongly positive and power compact, which yields existence and uniqueness of the principal eigenvalue and several variational characterizations. For spatially homogeneous coefficients, we establish the limit of the principal eigenvalue as the interval expands to $\mathbb R$ and identify it as the minimum of the principal Floquet exponents of the associated exponentially weighted periodic systems. To the best of our knowledge, this spectral theory is new even in \textbf{the scalar case}. We then apply these results to nonlinear systems. On bounded intervals, the sign of the principal eigenvalue gives a sharp dichotomy: solutions either converge to a unique positive time-periodic solution or vanish as time tends to infinity. We also prove convergence of positive periodic solutions as the interval expands. For the Cauchy problem on the whole real line, we characterize the leftward and rightward spreading speeds, which may differ for asymmetric dispersal kernels, and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for accelerated spreading in either direction. In particular, under irreducible coupling, accelerated spreading in one component induces accelerated spreading in all components in the same direction.
item.dc:creator: Hao Wu, Xiangdong Fang, Wan-Tong Li, Wenjie Ni

item.title: Sharp global well-posedness for the defocusing nonlinear wave equation outside a ball with radial data
item.description: arXiv:2611.30302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Omega=\mathbb{R}^3\setminus\overline{B(0,1)}$ and $3<p<5$. We prove sharp global well-posedness of the defocusing Dirichlet boundary value problem of nonlinear wave equation with radial data in the critical space $\dot H^{s_c}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(\Omega)\times \dot H^{s_c-1}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(\Omega)$, where $s_c=\frac32-\frac{2}{p-1}$, thereby improve the result in \cite{XuYangYou2025}. The proof combines the distorted Fourier transform in \cite{LiSZ:NLS,XuYang2024} with the energy--Morawetz estimate by Dodson in \cite{DodsonCubic2018,Dodson2018}.
item.dc:creator: Guixiang Xu

item.title: Optimal quantitative stability near the Coulomb fission threshold
item.description: arXiv:2611.30309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the optimal quadratic stability constant for the three-dimensional Coulomb liquid-drop energy at fixed volume, measured by the squared Fraenkel asymmetry. Let $M$ be the critical mass at which the energy of one ball equals the limiting energy of two infinitely separated balls of equal volume. We prove that, as $m$ approaches $M$ from below, the optimal constant satisfies $\Lambda(m)=(36\pi)^{1/3}(2^{1/3}-1)(1-m/M)+o(1-m/M)$. We further show that every almost optimal sequence with masses $m_n\to M$ from below is asymptotic in measure to a union of two equal-volume balls whose centers diverge. We also identify the corresponding perimeter and Coulomb-energy limits and give a necessary and sufficient criterion for almost optimality after rescaling to mass $M$. The proof combines a strict binding inequality for mass partitions, a local spectral gap at the critical ball, and a BV truncation argument for critical minimizing sequences. All results hold for arbitrary finite-perimeter competitors, without connectedness or boundary regularity assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Zijuan Gao, Chengxiang Zhang

item.title: The sharp mass threshold for the three-dimensional Riesz liquid-drop model near the Coulomb exponent
item.description: arXiv:2611.30329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the exact mass threshold of the three-dimensional liquid-drop model with repulsive kernel $|x-y|^{-s}$ in a two-sided neighborhood of the Coulomb exponent $s=1$. The infimum is attained precisely for $0<m\le\mstar$, with balls as the unique minimizers up to translation and null sets. Here $\mstar$ is the mass at which one ball and two equal balls at infinite separation have the same energy. We compute the first-order variation of this threshold at $s=1$. For $s>1$, a diameter bound proportional to the mass supplies a lower bound on the averaged planar slicing integral and yields a uniform mass bound. The resulting compactness and a uniform quadratic energy gap for finite-perimeter sets close in measure to a ball allow us to transfer the Coulomb classification to nearby exponents. At $m=\mstar$, every minimizing sequence has a subsequence asymptotic in measure to single balls or pairs of equal balls with diverging separation, with both alternatives realized by minimizing sequences. For $\mstar<m\le3\mstar/2$, only the separated pair occurs and the infimum is twice the energy of a half-mass ball. We also obtain the first-order change in interaction energy with respect to the exponent along subsequences of near-minimizers as $s\to1$ and $m\to m_*(1)$.
item.dc:creator: Zijuan Gao, Chengxiang Zhang

item.title: Normalized solutions of critical biharmonic equations on bounded domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.30362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the critical biharmonic equation with clamped boundary conditions and prescribed $L^2$ norm on a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge5$. For every sufficiently small mass, the constrained energy admits a local minimizer. We also obtain a second solution for masses in the closure of a measurable set having positive measure in every interval adjacent to zero. This holds on arbitrary smooth bounded domains when $N\ge8$ and, when $N=5,6,7$, under a condition involving the first clamped eigenvalue and a cutoff quotient. Explicit sufficient conditions are given and verified on balls. The proof combines a quantitative monotonicity argument with a norm estimate excluding loss of compactness.
item.dc:creator: Qilin Xie, Yelin Chen

item.title: Quasilinear elliptic equations involving asymptotically linear operators
item.dc:creator: Francescantonio Oliva, Francesco Petitta, Marcos Tadeu de Oliveira Pimenta, Sergio Segura de Le\'on

item.title: Towards a unified treatment of structured deformations theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.30539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Relying on the theory of $\mathcal B$ gradients, with $\mathcal B$ a $\mathbb C$-elliptic homogeneous linear partial differential operator of order $k$, with constant coefficients, we propose a method which allows to treat in a unified way the theories of structured deformations. Introducing the space of structured $\mathcal B$-deformations, $SD_{\mathcal B}$, we establish an integral-representation result for the associated energies, involving both bulk and surface contributions. Our approach relies on a direct application of the global method for relaxation, suitably adapted to the space of functions of $\mathcal B$-bounded variation.
item.dc:creator: Lorenza D'Elia, Elvira Zappale

item.title: Dirichlet does not imply Regularity for general elliptic operators in smooth domains
item.description:
arXiv:2611.30540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the upper half-space $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$, $n\geq2$, we show that there exists a real, diagonal, strongly elliptic matrix $A$ of bounded measurable coefficients, smooth in the interior of $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$ and continuous on its closure, such that for the elliptic operator $L=-\operatorname{div}A
abla$, the Dirichlet problem with data in $L^p$ is solvable, for every $p\in(1,\infty)$, but the Dirichlet-Regularity problem is not solvable for any $p\in(1,\infty)$. The counterexample has the following properties, in particular: 1. $A$ equals the identity matrix at the boundary and their $L^\infty$ distance in $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$ can be made arbitrarily small. 2. $A$ satisfies that $t|\partial_t A|^2$ is a Carleson measure. 3. $A$ fails to satisfy the Dahlberg-Kenig-Pipher condition only slightly, in the sense that for every $q>2$, $t^q|
abla A|^q rac{dxdt}{t}$ is a vanishing Carleson measure, but $t|
abla A|^2$ is not a Carleson measure. The counterexample resolves a long-standing question of C. Kenig.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Merlo, Mihalis Mourgoglou, Bruno Poggi

item.title: A sharp threshold in the Li--Lin open problem
item.dc:creator: Qihan He, Zongyan Lv

item.title: Geometry of ground states in the long-range Ising model
item.description: arXiv:2611.30604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the ground states of the ferromagnetic Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with long-range interactions and prescribed exterior data. We first show that the half-space configuration is a ground state, by means of a discrete calibration (which is the lattice counterpart of the calibrations of Cabr\'e and Pagliari for nonlocal minimal surfaces). In dimension $d\ge2$ and for positive kernels, the half-space configuration is the unique minimizer in every finite domain, and it is "stable" with respect to perturbations of the exterior datum whose energy is below half of a positive excitation gap. This rigidity has no counterpart in the continuum. For general exterior data and positive kernels, we show that along a monotone family the minimizer is unique except for finitely many data. This can be considered a "generic uniqueness result" that provides the discrete counterpart of a recent work of Dipierro, Fern\'andez-Real and Valdinoci in the continuum. We then introduce a pointwise notion, called perception, which is the lattice counterpart of the instability and stickiness phenomena for nonlocal minimal surfaces discovered by Dipierro, Savin and Valdinoci. We give a local criterion for the half-space configuration to be perceptive at a given site. Finally, we consider a box with exterior datum $+1$ above and below a slab and $-1$ on its sides. For fractional kernels with small exponent, the minimizer is $+1$ in the whole box, and its positive phase is connected. For short-range kernels, instead, the negative phase may enter the box, and the positive phase may be disconnected. Moreover, if the datum is $-1$ around the box and $+1$ only at distance two from it, the configuration identically $-1$ is perceptive at every boundary site of the box for fractional kernels with small exponent.
item.dc:creator: Serena Dipierro, Riccardo Sabbatini, Enrico Valdinoci

item.title: Scaling-invariant conditions for two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.30606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with either far-field vacuum or non-vacuum. Under suitable smallness conditions on explicitly constructed scaling-invariant initial quantities, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions involving initial vacuum states and large oscillations. The two far-field regimes present distinct analytical difficulties and require different approaches to the {\it a priori} estimates. Although the two smallness criteria have different forms, they arise from the same intrinsic scaling of the equations. Our results provide a unified scaling-invariant framework for the global well-posedness of strong solutions in both far-field regimes.
item.dc:creator: Lin Xu, Xin Zhong

item.title: Fundamental gaps of the restricted fractional Laplacian on thin planar convex domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.30610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the fundamental gap $\Gamma_s(\Omega)=\lambda_{2,s}(\Omega)-\lambda_{1,s}(\Omega)$ of the restricted Dirichlet fractional Laplacian for $0 < s < 1$. Building on the thin-rectangle estimates of Dyda and Kulczycki, we establish compact Mosco convergence of shifted quadratic forms and convergence of their eigenvalues on collapsing convex strips. This yields the next-order expansion, with exact coefficients, of each fixed eigenvalue of a thin rectangle. Let $G_s(\theta)$ be the infimum of $D^{2s}\Gamma_s(\Omega)$ over bounded open convex planar domains with $|\Omega|/D^2=\theta$, where $D$ denotes the diameter of $\Omega$. As $\theta\downarrow0$, we obtain $G_s(\theta)\sim\kappa_s\mathfrak{g}_{s+1/2}\theta$ for $0 < s < 1/2$, $G_{1/2}(\theta)\sim3\pi^2\gamma\theta\log(1/\theta)$, and $G_s(\theta)\sim3\pi^2\beta_s\theta^{2-2s}$ for $1/2 < s < 1$. The constants $\kappa_s$, $\gamma$, and $\beta_s$ are determined by the transverse interval ground state. On $I=(-1/2,1/2)$, let $\mathfrak{g}_t$ be the infimum of the fundamental gap of the restricted Dirichlet operator $(-\Delta)^t+V$ over convex $V\in C(\overline{I})$. For every $0 < t < 1$, this infimum is positive and is attained by a finite convex potential on $I$. Thin rectangles attain the optimal leading coefficient for $1/2\le s < 1$. For $0 < s < 1/2$, they do so exactly when the zero potential attains $\mathfrak{g}_{s+1/2}$. Finally, after diameter normalization, rescaling by $\theta^{-1}$ in a minimum-width direction, and suitable rotations and translations, the closures of asymptotically minimizing domains converge to $[-1/2,1/2]\times[0,1]$ in Hausdorff distance.
item.dc:creator: Rui Chen

item.title: Logarithmic stability from finite-time boundary measurements in an infinite slab
item.description: arXiv:2611.30630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove logarithmic stability for an inverse convection--diffusion problem in an infinite slab from finite-time partial boundary measurements. The data consist of boundary fluxes generated by a fixed temporal profile and varying spatial Dirichlet inputs. For coefficients with fixed interior support and uniform Sobolev bounds, the data determine the exterior derivative of the drift and a gauge-invariant reaction term with a logarithmic modulus. Prescribing the divergence gives separate stability for the drift and reaction coefficients. The input and observation patches may be arbitrary nonempty open subsets of the same or opposite faces. The proof combines a quantitative passage from finite-time responses to a stationary boundary map with a Runge approximation estimate in the measured $H^{3/2}$ input norm. The first step uses sectorial semigroups on the unbounded slab; the second transfers the partial data to a full boundary map on an interior domain, where magnetic stability estimates apply. We also prove conditional stability for boundary-touching supports and uniqueness from one encoded input with unknown initial state. A tracer-transport application identifies an incompressible velocity and a reaction-loss coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Yujian Zheng, Zhiwen Duan, Shiqi Jing

item.title: Modeling and analysis of a phase-field model for organic solar cells
item.description: arXiv:2611.30660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive and analyze a phase-field model describing the formation of the active layer of organic solar cells. The process combines phase separation of an electron donor (polymer) and an electron acceptor (non-fullerene acceptor) with evaporation of a solvent. Taking the macroscopic motion of the fluid into account, this results in a coupled system of incompressible Navier--Stokes, degenerate multispecies Cahn--Hilliard, and Allen--Cahn equations with cross-diffusion terms. We give a thermodynamically consistent derivation of the system and prove the existence of global-in-time weak solutions without any size constraints on the data. The solutions dissipate the total energy and require an ad-hoc variational formulation of the definition of the diffusion fluxes, which is made necessary by the degeneracy of the mobility matrix.
item.dc:creator: Jan-Frederik Pietschmann, Carmen Tretmans, Nicola Zamponi

item.title: A local-in-time quadratic functional for scalar conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2611.30663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a Glimm-type functional for scalar conservation laws, which is quadratic (w.r.t. the total variation of the initial datum), it controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions, and, differently than functionals with similar properties already present in the literature, it is purely local in time, meaning that it depends only on the present profile of the (approximate) solution (and not on its past or future evolution).
item.dc:creator: Egor Baitenov, Stefano Modena

item.title: The cost functional for hyperbolic systems of conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2611.30664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For hyperbolic systems of conservation laws (without any genuine nonlinearity of linear degeneracy assumption on the flux) we construct a quadratic interaction functional, which controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions and it is local in time. This extends the analysis of [3] from scalar conservation laws to $n \times n$ systems.
item.dc:creator: Egor Baitenov, Stefano Modena

item.title: Microlocal and global smoothing effect of variable coefficient ZK-type operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.30665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study the smoothing effect of a class of Zakharov-Kuznetsov (ZK) equations, which generalize the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation to higher dimensions. Specifically, we consider linear evolution equations generated by ZK-type operators with variable coefficients, and we study both their microlocal and global smoothing effects under suitable conditions on the coefficients of the operator. Our analysis requires a detailed study of the geometric properties of the Hamiltonian flow associated with the operator under consideration. These properties allow us to prove a dispersive and a strong smoothing effect associated with the Cauchy problem in question: under suitable moment conditions on the initial datum, the solution becomes smooth in space for positive times in a finite time interval.
item.dc:creator: Serena Federico, Davide Tramontana

item.title: On the Unique Identification of Finitely Many Radial Heat Sources
item.description: arXiv:2611.30686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate an inverse source problem for the heat equation in $\R^d$ ($d\geq1$), in which the source is a finite positive linear combination of translates of a known real-valued radial Schwartz profile with nonzero total mass. Both the locations and strengths of the sources are to be identified from the observations of time traces at finitely many spatial points over an arbitrary nonempty open positive-time interval. For $d\geq2$, we prove that the sharp universal measurement threshold is $dN+1$: every set of $dN+1$ measurement points in affine general position uniquely identifies every source configuration with at most $N$ locations. For $d=1$, we prove that two distinct measurement points uniquely identify every finite source configuration, independently of the number of sources, and that this count is sharp. The analysis relies on an equivalence between equality of heat traces and equality of weighted distance measures, and then employs perpendicular-bisector hyperplanes to resolve geometric ambiguities. We also establish identification guarantees using $d+1$ measurement points: clustered designs under a reference-distance separation condition, adaptive designs for arbitrary configurations, and any fixed affinely independent design for almost every location configuration, uniformly over all positive strengths.
item.dc:creator: Bangti Jin, Zhi Zhou

item.title: Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Operators: Strict Monotonicity and Asymptotic Behavior
item.description: arXiv:2611.30689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the properties of the generalized principal eigenvalue for a coupled local/nonlocal operator. First, we establish sufficient conditions to guarantee strict monotonicity properties, obtaining weaker hypotheses than those currently available in the literature for nonlocal operators. Next, we establish several results concerning the asymptotic behavior of this generalized eigenvalue, along with the convergence of the corresponding eigenfunctions. These results are very useful for the study of nonlinear problems. Our findings reveal novel phenomena that are not present in purely local or purely nonlocal cases. The main mathematical difficulty lies in the fact that the generalized eigenvalue does not always admit an eigenfunction, in addition to the inherent technicalities of the considered coupling.
item.dc:creator: Willian Cintra, J\^onatas Peralta, Antonio Su\'arez

item.title: Kinetic transfer or regularity in any dimension from uncertainty inequalities on the real line
item.description: arXiv:2611.30703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this short note is to show that one dimensional uncertainty inequalities easily induce transfer of regularity inequalities in kinetic equations in any dimension.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Auscher (LMO)

item.title: A Keller--Segel Chemotaxis Model on One-Dimensional Moving Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.30752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a one-dimensional Keller--Segel system on an interval whose boundary moves according to a prescribed contracting law. The boundary motion makes the problem genuinely nonautonomous and destroys the mass conservation available on fixed domains. A time-dependent change of variables, combined with a time reparametrization, reduces the problem to a semilinear system on a fixed interval with time-independent principal part and nonautonomous transport terms. We prove global well-posedness and regularity of weak solutions, and we show that the contraction of the domain yields a uniform bound on the total mass. For the long-time dynamics, our main tool is a singular Gronwall type inequality with an exponentially damped kernel, for which we provide a self-contained version with explicit decay rate and constants, tailored to our setting; under a small gain condition on the boundary velocities, it yields dissipativity with an explicit exponential decay rate, which cannot be obtained from the classical inequality of Henry. With it we prove the existence of the minimal pullback attractor in the universe of families of bounded sets, on the moving domain and then on the fixed rescaled reference domains. Finally, numerical simulations on contracting domains illustrate the effect of the boundary motion on cell aggregation.
item.dc:creator: Jackeline C. Huaccha Neyra, John Matos Ascona, Lizet Santa Cruz Calder\'on, Heraclio L\'opez-L\'azaro

item.title: On the Fourier Analysis of the Einstein-Klein-Gordon System: Limiting Behaviour of the Fourier Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.30759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the problem of computing the Fourier coefficients associated with the spherically symmetric massless-scalar field system in $(1+3)$ dimensions initiated in [10]. We rigorously derive computationally efficient formulas for these coefficients and then use them to establish their asymptotic behavior as the mode numbers tend to infinity, including the explicit determination of the leading-order coefficients. Our approach builds on the method developed in [12] and relies on two powerful algorithms for hypergeometric summation, due to Zeilberger and Gosper. These algorithms enable us to systematically derive first-order linear recurrence relations and obtain closed-form discrete antiderivatives respectively for intricate hypergeometric sequences that arise in our analysis.
item.dc:creator: Athanasios Chatzikaleas, Jacques Smulevici

item.title: Isolated singularities of weak solutions to the quasilinear Lane-Emden equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study isolated singularities of nonnegative weak solutions to $-\Delta_pu=u^q$ in $B_1\setminus\{0\}$, where $\Delta_p$ is the $p$-Laplacian, $1<p<n$, and $n(p-1)/(n-p)<q<np/(n-p)-1$. We prove that either the origin is a removable singularity or $u(x)\sim K_{n,p,q}|x|^{-p/(q+1-p)}$ as $x\to0$, where $K_{n,p,q}>0$ is an explicit constant depending only on $n,p,q$. The result holds without radial symmetry or an a priori growth assumption. The proof combines a removability criterion with a rigidity theorem for positive solutions in $\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$ satisfying two-sided power bounds. To handle the infinite $p$-Dirichlet energy at the singularity, we construct a continuous Steiner deformation that fixes all sufficiently high superlevel sets. The resulting energy comparison yields radial symmetry of the blow-up limits.
item.dc:creator: Meiqing Xu, Hui Yang

item.title: Unique continuation and its failure for the Monge--Amp\`ere equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study unique continuation for Alexandrov solutions with common Monge--Amp\`ere density bounded above and below. In the plane, we prove that agreement on an open set forces global equality. For every bounded domain \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) with \(n\ge3\), we construct two distinct uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}(\Omega)\) solutions that agree on a nonempty open subset of \(\Omega\).
item.dc:creator: XiaoRui Lu

item.title: Uniform velocity support for the repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system
item.description: arXiv:2611.30914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proves that the velocity support of the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system remains uniformly bounded for all time for nonnegative initial data in \(C_c^1(\mathbb R^6)\). The proof establishes uniform bounds on a weighted fifth-order energy moment and an associated fourth-order force integral by exploiting the relative motion of particle pairs. On intervals where the target particle moves sufficiently fast relative to the expansion, these estimates give a summable bound for the current in its energy identity. This bound yields uniform control of the velocity support.
item.dc:creator: Zhaopeng Wang

item.title: The sharp Trudinger--Moser exponent in Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.30915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the sharp Trudinger--Moser inequality in the fractional Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces $W^{s,p}$, $0 < s < 1$, at the critical index $sp=N$, including the endpoint.
