Our approach combines the weak differential calculus and the Bochner inequality available in the $\mathrm{RCD}^*(-K,N)$ setting with suitable auxiliary function arguments, extending classical gradient estimate techniques to nonsmooth spaces. The resulting estimate is valid for all exponents $\alpha,\beta>0$ and all $N\in[1,\infty)$, with no dimensional case distinction and with explicit constants. As an application, we prove a quantitative, asymptotic Liouville-type theorem on $\mathrm{RCD}^*(0,N)$ spaces: for positive solutions that are bounded above and below by fixed positive constants, the normalized gradients $|\nabla f|/f$ and $|\nabla h|/h$ are bounded by a quantity that is of order $\max\{\alpha,\beta\}$ and hence tends to zero as the exponents tend to zero (with comparable size). We also explain why the method gives no rigidity for large exponents, which is consistent with, but does not prove, the existence of nonconstant solutions there. These results generalize corresponding results from the smooth Riemannian setting and contribute to the study of nonlinear elliptic systems on spaces with synthetic Ricci curvature lower bounds.
item.dc:creator: Sujit Bhattacharyya

item.title: Derivation of a linearly elastic elliptic membrane shell theory in the framework of magnetoelasticity
item.description: arXiv:2608.30445v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Starting from a three-dimensional model of linearized magnetoelasticity, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of a thin shell as its thickness approaches zero. Our analysis focuses on a family of linearly elastic elliptic membrane shells. Using $\Gamma$-convergence, we rigorously derive a two-dimensional linear magnetoelastic shell model and establish its relationship to the original three-dimensional model in terms of the convergence of minimizers.
item.dc:creator: Trung Hieu Giang

item.title: Positive normalized solutions for a singular regularized $p(x)$-Laplacian Dirichlet problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.20778v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a singular Dirichlet problem driven by a regularized $p(x)$-Laplacian under a prescribed modular constraint. We construct nonnegative constrained minimizers for nonsingular approximating problems and, under the stated variational and boundary-control hypotheses, obtain a positive normalized weak solution as the reaction regularization vanishes. The approximation preserves the prescribed modular and yields subsequential strong Sobolev convergence of the states together with convergence of their constraint multipliers, while the gradient regularization remains fixed. Finally, we present a normalized singular problem on the unit disk as an illustrative example.
item.dc:creator: Mustafa Avci

item.title: Asymptotically H\"{o}lder gradient regularity for degenerate or singular parabolic normalized $ p$-Laplace equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.34855v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study bounded viscosity solutions of the degenerate or singular parabolic equation \[ u_t-|Du|^{\gamma}\Delta_p^{\mathrm{N}}u=f \qquad \text{in } Q_1, \] where \[ \Delta_p^{\mathrm{N}}u := \Delta u+(p-2) \left\langle D^2u\frac{Du}{|Du|}, \frac{Du}{|Du|} \right\rangle, \qquad -1<\gamma<\infty,\quad 1<p<\infty, \] and $f\in C^0(Q_1)\cap L^\infty(Q_1)$. Given any prescribed $\alpha\in(0,1)$, we prove that there exists $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,\alpha)>0$ such that \[ |p-2|+|\gamma|\leq\varepsilon \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1+\alpha,\frac{1+\alpha}{2}}(Q_1). \] In particular, the spatial gradient H\"older exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to $ 1 $ as $(p,\gamma)\to(2,0)$. This extends the result of Andrade and Santos (Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations \textbf{61}, Paper No. 196, 2022) for $\gamma=0$ to the joint regime $(p,\gamma)\to(2,0)$ and answers affirmatively the question raised in Remark~1.1 therein.
item.dc:creator: Jiangwen Wang, Yini Zhang, Feida Jiang

item.title: Optimal convergence rates in homogenization of Monge-Amp\`ere equations with periodic measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.03269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates in periodic homogenization of Monge--Amp\`ere equations, allowing the microscopic measure to be singular or degenerate. Let $\mu$ be a nonnegative $\mathbb Z^n$-periodic Borel measure with $\mu(\mathbb T^n)=1$, and set $\mu_\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon^n\mu(E/\varepsilon)$. On a bounded convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, let $u^\varepsilon$ and $u$ be the convex solutions of \[ \det D^2u^\varepsilon=F(x,x/\varepsilon)\,\mu_\varepsilon,\qquad\det D^2u=\overline{F}(x) \] with the same Dirichlet data, where the coefficient $F$ is bounded, uniformly positive, and periodic in its second variable, and $\overline F(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^n}F(x,y)\,d\mu(y)$. For $m=0,1$ and $0<\alpha\leq1$, we prove \[ \|u^\varepsilon-u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\leq C\varepsilon^{m+\alpha},\qquad \forall\,0<\varepsilon\leq1, \] provided that $u\in C^{m+2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ and $F(\cdot,y)\in C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uniformly in $y$. These exponents are optimal in their respective regularity scales, and the constant $C$ is independent of the distribution of the microscopic measure. In particular, the estimates include the optimal quadratic rate for general periodic measures. Our proof of the lower-order estimate ($m=0$) relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for periodic correctors. For the higher-order estimate ($m=1$), we introduce a constrained Monge--Amp\`ere problem that produces convex approximations with prescribed cell averages. This construction captures the cancellation in the third-order corrector expansion without uniform Hessian bounds for the correctors.
item.dc:creator: Tianling Jin, YanYan Li, Hung V. Tran, Xushan Tu

item.title: On blow-up for the supercritical defocusing nonlinear scalar wave equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19757v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study finite-time singularity formation for the scalar defocusing nonlinear wave equation $-\partial_t^2u+\Delta u=u^p$. First, for fixed $d\geq4$ and odd $p\geq3$, we prove a conditional blow-up result under the assumption that the leading-order relativistic Euler system admits a smooth self-similar imploding profile whose associated normalized coefficients satisfy quantitative analytic radius conditions. Second, we verify both the existence of the profile and the analytic radius conditions in dimensions four and five for all sufficiently large odd $p$. Using the finite speed of propagation, we then obtain a threshold $p_0$, independent of the dimension, such that for every $d\geq4$ and every odd $p\geq p_0$, there exist smooth, compactly supported, real-valued initial data whose solutions blow up in finite time. The proof combines three ingredients: a normalized formulation that separates the leading periodic oscillation from the unknown modulation, the growth of the spatial analytic radius induced by an outgoing property, and frequency-dependent matrix multipliers that control the cumulative growth caused by the periodic linearized potential.
item.dc:creator: Feng Shao, Dongyi Wei, Zhifei Zhang

item.title: Threshold Attainment and Sharp Asymptotics for $L^p$-Perturbed Moser--Trudinger Functionals on $\mathbb{R}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.29402v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the critical Moser--Trudinger supremum \[ S(\lambda,p)=\sup_{\|u\|_{H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)}\le1} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\bigl(e^{4\pi u^2}-1-\lambda|u|^p\bigr)\,dx, \qquad p\ge2, \] Chen--Jiang--Lu--Zhu gave the first classification of attainment away from the thresholds across the full range of $p$. We prove attainment at both thresholds for $p=2$ and at the unique threshold for each $2<p\le4$. At and above the upper quadratic threshold, $S(\lambda,2)=4\pi e^{1-2\gamma_{\mathrm E}}$, Nguyen's concentration level, where $\gamma_{\mathrm E}$ is the Euler--Mascheroni constant. At each endpoint, the centred radial extremals form a compact set and their $L^p$ masses determine the slope from within the attainment interval. For fixed $p>4$, we obtain the expansion \[ S(\lambda,p)=4\pi+\mathcal C_p\lambda^{-2/(p-4)} +D_p\lambda^{-4/(p-4)}+o\bigl(\lambda^{-4/(p-4)}\bigr), \qquad \lambda\to\infty. \] Here $\mathcal C_p$ is the maximum of a limiting problem at unit $L^2$ mass, and $D_p$ selects the limiting profiles. For fixed $\lambda$ above the quartic threshold $\lambda_*(4)$, we prove \[ \lim_{p\downarrow4}(p-4)\log\bigl(S(\lambda,p)-4\pi\bigr) =2\log\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}}{\lambda}<0, \] where $\lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is determined by the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg constant. An exact radial transformation extends these results to every planar norm.
item.dc:creator: Kaiwen Guo, Yanjun Liu

item.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
item.description: arXiv:2611.02886v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Auscher (LMO)

item.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
item.description: arXiv:2611.14315v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lema\^{i}tre--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.
item.dc:creator: Xueyi Yu

item.title: Strong and weak mean value sets for elliptic operators: uniqueness and counterexamples
item.description: arXiv:2611.15988v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. In the Fermi Lectures, Caffarelli described an obstacle problem construction of analogous averaging sets for symmetric uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. For such an operator with bounded measurable coefficients in dimension $n \ge 2,$ fix a center $x_0$ and a volume $V > 0,$ and let $E$ be the corresponding canonical set. We prove that a bounded open set $D$ of volume $V$ containing $x_0$ satisfies the mean value inequality at $x_0$ for every integrable subsolution on $D$ if and only if $E \subset D \subset \operatorname{int}\overline{E}.$ In particular, every such strong mean value set agrees with $E$ almost everywhere. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison. Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ''mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume contains the entire unit sphere and has a hole of positive measure inside the unit ball.
item.dc:creator: Niles Armstrong, Ivan Blank

item.title: Eventual Collisional Relaxation After Large Echo-Driven Amplification in a Weakly Collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System
item.description:
arXiv:2611.16761v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the weakly collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system near a Maxwellian equilibrium and construct global classical solutions exhibiting large transient growth before eventual collisional relaxation. The main mechanism is a nonlinear plasma-echo cascade which remains effective up to the enhanced-dissipation time scale $t\sim
u^{- rac13}$, producing norm inflation of size larger than $
u^{-1}$ from arbitrarily small $
u$-dependent perturbations. At the same time, the nonzero spatial modes decay at the enhanced-dissipation scale $e^{-\mathsf{r}
u^{ rac13}t}$, while the zero mode relaxes at the thermal scale $e^{-
u t}$. The estimates also reveal a sharp contrast in the smoothing effects before and after the collisional time scale $t\sim 
u^{-1}$. As a consequence, our construction gives explicit upper bounds on the Sobolev and Gevrey stability thresholds: perturbations of the corresponding $
u$-dependent sizes can still trigger severe echo-driven amplification before collisional dissipation becomes dominant at the critical time scale $t\sim
u^{- rac13}$.
item.dc:creator: Luo Yue

item.title: Mixed Inner Variation and Global Hessian Integrability for Degenerate Monge-Amp\`ere Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17088v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the global Hessian integrability for nonzero convex solutions of the degenerate Monge-Amp\`ere equations $\det D^2u=M(-u)^p$ with zero boundary values on arbitrary bounded convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$ in the global Lipschitz regime $p>n-2$. We establish global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimates for every $0<\varepsilon<\min\{(p-n+2)/n,1\}$ and determine the optimal range of $\varepsilon$ in dimension two and on rectangular boxes. The flat faces of rectangular boxes and their intersections impose upper bounds on the admissible exponents of global Hessian integrability. A new input in the proof for general dimensions is a Caccioppoli-type estimate for the boundary Hessian mass using vector fields arising from a mixed second inner variation. For the sharp higher integrability result in the plane, we use the combined hodograph-Legendre transform to control the curvature of level sets.
item.dc:creator: Nam Q. Le

item.title: Classification of critical points of heat kernels on flat tori and Riemann theta functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.19067v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any two-dimensional flat torus $E_\tau:=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathbb Z\tau)$ and any $t>0$, we prove that the heat kernel $p_{\tau}(z,t)$ has either four or six critical points on $z\in E_{\tau}$ (i.e., including four trivial critical points and at most one pair of nontrivial critical points). This is interestingly consistent with Lin-Wang's remarkable result (Ann. Math. 2010) for the Green function. The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given. In particular, we resolve a conjecture of Luo and Wei (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 2022).
item.dc:creator: Zhijie Chen, Chen-Gang Long, Shihong Zhang

item.title: On the Cauchy problem for $\sigma$-evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients via upper decay indicators
item.description: arXiv:2611.19532v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, the first main goal is to investigate the Cauchy problem for the linear $\sigma$-evolution equation $$ u_{tt}+a^2(t)(-\Delta)^\sigma u+b(t)u_t+m^2(t)u=0, $$ where propagation speed, damping term and mass are time-dependent functions. Under suitable assumptions on the interaction among these coefficients, we not only derive decay estimates for the solution and its derivatives in terms of the effective parabolic time scale $\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(s,t):=\int_s^t a^2(\tau)/b(\tau) d\tau$, but also conclude the additional decay induced by the mass term and the upper decay indicators of the initial data. Especially, one can recognize that the time-derivative estimate for solutions exhibits a competition between $m^2(t)$ and $a^2(t)\left(1+\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(0,t)\right)^{-1}$. For the corresponding semi-linear problem with the nonlinear term $|u|^p$, we also establish global (in time) existence of small data solutions fulfilling decay estimates, coming from the mass factor $\exp\left(-\int_0^t m^2(\tau)/b(\tau)d\tau\right)$, under the same assumptions on these coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Duc An Phan, Tuan Anh Dao, The Anh Cung

item.title: Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for Hamilton--Jacobi equations with supercritical viscosity
item.description: arXiv:2611.20638v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $\sigma>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^\sigma\Delta u_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{\sigma-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.
item.dc:creator: Gengyu Liu, Zibo Wang, Jianlu Zhang

item.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation with boundary in higher dimensions I
item.description: arXiv:2611.20647v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study isolated boundary singularities of positive solutions of the scalar-flat boundary Yamabe equation. We prove the critical upper bound for general smooth metrics in dimensions $3\le n\le17$ and for Euclidean domains with smooth boundary in dimensions $3\le n\le22$. For general metrics, this range extends to $n=18$ when the conformal metric is complete near the singularity. In every dimension, the critical upper bound implies removability or a matching lower bound and convergence to a unique flat Fowler solution with a positive power rate. Sharpness of these dimension ranges will be established in a subsequent paper.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Liao

item.title: A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.22208v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fr\'echet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point. Furthermore, we prove the propagation of $H^2$-regularity for sufficiently regular initial data.
item.dc:creator: Keyu Li, Hui Huang

item.title: Infinite cascades for the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the square torus
item.description: arXiv:2611.24906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For each finite $s>1$ we construct a solution of the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the square two-torus with initial data in $H^s$ whose $H^s$ norm tends to infinity as $t\to+\infty$. The growth can be arbitrarily slow. More precisely, the squared norm agrees, up to a bounded error at all positive times, with the number of selected axial frequencies $K_j$ for which $K_j^s\le t$. The central construction couples a finite tree of orthogonal frequency pairs to a finite-dimensional family of one-dimensional solutions of the same equation. Each transfer leaves a nonvanishing Fourier coefficient on the horizontal axis. Control on an entire half-line allows successive transfers to retain the coefficients produced earlier. At and above the index two, we match the second-order normal frequency shift separately on each triangle using harmonics of the axial solution. For every fixed $2<s<\infty$ we also obtain a solution for which $\log\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\asymp\sqrt{\log t/\log\log t}$ at every sufficiently large time.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen

item.title: Interior $W^{2,p}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.25242v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we extend Caffarelli's interior $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,\alpha}$ regularity theory for the Monge-Amp\`ere equation to the $k$-Hessian equation, $3\leq k\leq n-1$, under sharp Sobolev or H\"older assumptions on the solution. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we establish $W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,1}$ regularity for continuous $k$-convex solutions; the exponent $1$ is optimal even for constant density. Higher interior regularity holds under either of two assumptions: $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,k(k-1)/2}$, or $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,\beta}$ for some $1-2/k<\beta<1$. Under either assumption, if the density is positive and continuous, then $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,p}$ for every $1<p<\infty$; if the density is positive and belongs to $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\alpha}$, then $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,\alpha}$ for $0<\alpha<1$. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we also establish global $W^{2,1}$ regularity on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex $C^{1,1}$ domains with $C^{1,1}$ boundary values.
item.dc:creator: Yasheng Lyu

item.title: Global Strong Solutions and Large-Time Behavior for Radial Compressible Navier-Stokes Flow with Density-Dependent Viscosities on a Disk and in the Plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.27108v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations admit a unique global strong solution for arbitrarily large compatible radial initial data without swirl and with density bounded away from zero, both on a disk with a no-slip wall and in the whole plane. The shear and second viscosities have a common density exponent between one half and one, inclusive. For each exponent in this range, the bulk viscosity coefficient may take any nonnegative value. This is the full range allowed by nonnegative viscous dissipation in a two-dimensional Newtonian fluid with positive shear viscosity. Every pressure exponent greater than or equal to one is admissible. In particular, these results apply to Marche's viscous shallow water equations on a flat bottom in the absence of rotation, bottom friction, and capillarity. These equations retain the positive second viscosity derived from free-surface flow and thus fall outside the Bresch-Desjardins relation. The density remains uniformly bounded above and away from zero for all time. On the disk, the density and velocity converge exponentially in the Sobolev norm of order three to the spatial mean of the density and to zero, respectively. In the plane, the solution converges in the same norm to the prescribed far-field state with positive density and zero velocity. The same conclusions hold for classes of non-power viscosities, including laws with different growth rates at low and high density.
item.dc:creator: Kexin Li

item.title: Spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem
item.description: arXiv:2509.08588v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $\lambda_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $\lambda_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.
item.dc:creator: Yao Wan

item.title: Classification of fractional, singular Yamabe metrics on a twice punctured sphere I
item.description: arXiv:2511.05225v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Delaunay metrics form a family of conformally flat, constant fractional Q-curvature metrics on a twice-punctured sphere. They are all (after a M\"obius transformation) rotationally symmetric and periodic, and admit several elegant variational descriptions. We prove that, when s is close to but less than 1, any complete, conformally flat constant Q-curvature metric on a twice-punctured sphere is a Delaunay metric. Along the way, we prove a sharp a priori bound for the conformal factor of these metrics, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Henrique Andrade, Azahara DelaTorre, Jo\~ao Marcos do \`O, Jesse Ratzkin, Juncheng Wei

item.title: Two energy methods for distributed port-Hamiltonian systems and their application to stability analysis
item.description: arXiv:2511.23336v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop two local energy methods for distributed parameter port-Hamiltonian (pH) systems on one-dimensional spatial domains. The methods are applied to derive a characterization of exponential stability directly in terms of the energy passing through the boundary over a given time horizon. The resulting condition is verified for a network of vibrating strings where existing sufficient conditions cannot be applied. Moreover, we use a local energy method to study the short-time behavior of pH systems with boundary damping which was recently studied in the context of hypocoercivity.
item.dc:creator: Marco Roschkowski, Hannes Gernandt

item.title: Rotationally symmetric translating solitons of fully nonlinear extrinsic geometric flows: Classification and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2512.23623v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study rotationally symmetric translating solitons of fully non-linear extrinsic geometric flows in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ driven by positive $\alpha$-homogeneous curvature functions, building on Rengaswami's classification of bowl-type translators. For positive ends at infinity and every $\alpha>0$, we derive two correction terms beyond the leading order in the nondegenerate case and the growth rate in each degenerate regime. Imposing the translator equation across the neck on a signed extension of the curvature function, we construct catenoidal translators and classify their continuations according to a branch of the rotational level set. These yield complete embedded translators or maximal pieces, for which we determine the regularity at each transition and the shrinking-neck asymptotics; each alternative is realized in a model family of curvature functions. As applications of the tangency principle, we obtain rigidity and nonexistence results governed by the global geometry of the bowl-type solutions. When the bowl is entire, it is unique up to vertical translation among convex translators with a single graphical end asymptotic to it (also under a weighted condition in the strictly convex case), and its existence rules out both convex translating graphs over bounded domains that blow up at the boundary and entire ones growing uniformly faster or slower than the bowl. When the bowl is not entire, it may have finite height for $\alpha>1$; in this setting, any strictly convex translating graph over a ball that is continuous up to the boundary and has vertical tangent planes there is necessarily a bowl of finite height.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Torres Santaella

item.title: Approximate Controllability of the generalized Burgers-Huxley equation in one dimension
item.description: arXiv:2606.31968v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The generalized Burgers-Huxley (GBH) equation is a prototype model that describes the interplay among reaction, convection, and diffusion. In this article, we explore the controllability of this model by means of an interior control supported in an arbitrary non-empty open subset of the domain. We establish that the GBH equation is not globally approximately controllable in a given time. However, it is possible to steer the system from any steady state to an arbitrarily small neighborhood of another steady state in some suitable time by means of a localized interior control, provided that both steady states lie in the same connected component of the set of steady states.
item.dc:creator: Aman Patel, Mohmedmunavvar Mubarak Bapu, Mrinmay Biswas

item.title: Pinchoff by surface diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2608.21882v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Since Nichols and Mullins analysed the instability of cylindrical wires in 1965, numerical and asymptotic studies have predicted a self-similar neck at pinchoff under surface diffusion. Yet even the existence of a finite-time singularity for the flow of a smooth closed surface has remained open. We construct the first such examples, and establish their stability, modulo a finite-dimensional space. The same shrinking neck closes the central hole of an embedded torus in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and separates the lobes of a genus-zero dumbbell. In both cases the surface remains embedded until the singular time $T$ and converges smoothly away from the pinching point. Writing $A(t)$ for the waist radius and $r(z,t)$ for the radius near the neck, we prove that $A(t)=\{4\mu(T-t)\}^{1/4}(1+o(1)), \quad A(t)^{-1}r(A(t)\zeta,t) \longrightarrow U(\zeta) \quad\text{in }C^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}).$ The profile $U$ above is also for the first time rigorously constructed here. It was numerically computed by Wong-Miksis-Voorhees-Davis, and identified by Bernoff-Bertozzi-Witelski as the ground state of a family of conical shrinkers. Our proof also yields a general compactification and stability criterion for fourth-order geometric flows that admit positive symmetric conical shrinkers.
item.dc:creator: Glen Wheeler

item.title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
item.description: arXiv:2610.27343v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\chi_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,\chi_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $\xi_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R$, we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2} \Phi_L(u) e^{izu} du, \] where $\Phi_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ \Phi_L(u) := \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \xi_L \left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu} ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $\xi_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $\Lambda_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge \Lambda_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $\Lambda_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $\Lambda_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $\Lambda_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $\Lambda_L\le95241/320000=0.297628125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Freire, Cristian Gonz\'alez-Riquelme, Claudio Mu\~noz, Felipe Poblete, Vicente Salinas

item.title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32534v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $\mu$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(\mu)$, then $\mu$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.
item.dc:creator: John Hoffman

item.title: Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements of the Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.33346v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and we obtain its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range $1<p<\infty$. We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when $1<p<n$, a weighted exponential integrability of Trudinger type when $p=n$, where the Hardy term is replaced by its Leray logarithmic correction, and a weighted H\"older seminorm when $p>n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for $F_o$-radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction and, for $1<p\le n$, on a splitting of the transformed function into its $F_o$-spherical mean and a mean-free part. Since $F^2$ is not a quadratic form unless $F$ is induced by a scalar product, the reduction of the radial part through spherical harmonics, used in the Euclidean case, is not available; we control the radial part directly, through a convexity inequality for $F^p$ with a quadratic remainder and sharp one-dimensional estimates, and the mean-free part through a Poincar\'e inequality on the boundary of the Wulff shape. For $p>n$ we use an anisotropic Morrey representation formula.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppina di Blasio, Giovanni Pisante, Georgios Psaradakis

item.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the two-component modified Camassa-Holm system with step-like boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.39938v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a Riemann--Hilbert formalism for the Cauchy problem for the two-component modified Camassa--Holm (2-mCH) system on the real line under non-zero step-like boundary conditions. Starting from the corresponding Lax pair, we carry out the direct spectral analysis and establish the analytic, symmetry, and asymptotic properties of the eigenfunctions and spectral data determined by the initial conditions. These results are then used to formulate right and left matrix Riemann--Hilbert problems and derive parametric formulas for reconstructing both components. These formulas also use a transported profile determined by the initial ratio of the two momenta. Under suitable regularity and positivity assumptions, we show that a solution of the right Riemann--Hilbert problem, together with this profile, yields a local solution of the 2-mCH system. For a common constant background, we construct a family of smooth reflectionless solutions associated with a single pair of discrete eigenvalues. The scalar soliton, obtained when the profile vanishes, is the only travelling wave in this family.
item.dc:creator: Iryna Karpenko, Dmitry Shepelsky, Gerald Teschl
